body:
Greg's current operative decisions, as rules. His words and sources: greg-decisions-provenance, cited [Pn].

LANDING AND REVIEW [P1-P6]. The rule is CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md "Commit and push", condition 1.
- A Note never blocks. A Low does not block; fixing it is optional, and an unfixed Low is filed as its own item. Medium and higher is fixed and reviewed again.
- When the gate is green on the exact input, the review pair has nothing of Medium or higher, and the tasks carry their evidence, agents commit and the integration owner pushes without asking Greg. Authority text still needs conditions (a), (b) and (c).
- Master's text governs [P6]: the instruction files on origin/master, not the copy a session received at start. If they differ, follow master, name the difference in your record, and do not stop to ask Greg. Ask him only when master's rules truly leave the decision to him; waiting on him for what the rules already decide blocks all work (it once held a green, reviewed landing ~4 h). Item: w-413f25141785.

WORKING WITHOUT ASKING [P7-P12]
- Agents may improve the rules; work must run smoothly. Do not hold work for Greg; make and record the agents' own decisions.
- Take questions on priorities, scope, design, sequencing or rule readings to the architects, the integration owner, Engram::Fable or Engram::Advisor, who relays Greg. Keep processing mail; never block on a question to Greg.
- Through Engram::Advisor, once per new requirement, tell him when a restart is needed or the environment fails. Report only significant progress, blockers and new restart needs; ask him nothing.
- Send decisions once sent "for objection" as information, and act on them. An objection from him, by any route, still stops or reverts them.
- Routine, reversible tracker and coordination decisions, including done, cancel and supersede on evidence, need no confirmation from Greg and no per-session confirmation ceremony [P12]. Do not reopen items already corrected merely to recreate approval (Advisor, with P12).
- [P11] The integration owner may install the latest landed UI into ui/dist after confirming its exact source and build and normal scope, then report the deployed version and verification to Engram::Advisor. Other deploys still need Greg's word.

TERMAL RESTARTS: agents choose the timing; Greg performs the restart (settled 2026-10-02 23:55Z) [P23-P26]
- When an installed build carries fixes agents need, the coordinator picks a recoverable boundary: no full gate running, no review-pair children in flight, no recognised test turn mid-run. A quick check of the implementers is enough.
- It then sends Engram::Advisor "restart now" with the build hash, the master commit and the reason. A signal without "now" is information only; Greg waits for "restart now".
- Work never stops to wait for a restart or a boundary. Nobody holds or reserves a window for it.
- No agent stops or starts the host process. Engram agents may restart Engram; that is Engram's matter.
- Greg restarts with `cargo run --release` in the master checkout, which rebuilds target/release/termal.exe from master's source and replaces any installed binary there, with no backup. So push a landing to master before the restart signal. An installed-hash vs running-build mismatch afterwards is expected.
- A restart kills processes launched from agent sessions, gates included. Each owner then settles interrupted runs with `recover`, reruns them, and re-spawns interrupted delegations on the same freeze.
- Applies now; the CLAUDE.md wording is item w-5aa79f5c0654.

PROCESS DIRECTION [P13-P16]
- Finish the tool fixes first, then simplify; [P13] is not an instruction to change rules now.
- Not simplification targets: a base move with a new gate and pair (normal work), and many review rounds (they find real bugs). Filing Medium findings instead of blocking: undecided, leaning no; do not pursue unless Greg raises it.
- Smoother work comes from architecture (better composition, isolation), not from loosening the process. Prefer narrow seams, so a feature touches few files and reviewers have a small surface. Land smaller changes more often.
- Two cheap checks [P16]. The other architect checks a design ruling that changes a contract before anyone implements it; the author asks and names what he did not read; it is a static reading against the source, noted on the item, not a review pair. Before editing product code for such a ruling, the implementer writes the test it names and runs it on the unchanged code; if it does not fail as predicted, he stops and reports, and the ruling is corrected first. Neither check grants authority or replaces the gate, the review pair or the acceptance evaluation.
- Not yet discussed with Greg: the evidence chain and same-turn evaluation; the length of the commit-rule text; accumulated source-mutation obligations.

NO LEGACY SUPPORT [P17-P18]
- When new functionality replaces old, the old is removed; the two are not kept side by side. No bridges between versions: no adapter, fallback or translation layer whose job is to carry V1 into V2 into V3.
- Applying it (Architect1's reading): a design that introduces a replacement includes removing what it replaces, in the same work or as a filed item it names. "The uncovered cases keep the old behaviour" is the side-by-side arrangement; do not design it in. No compatibility branch that detects the old form and routes it to old code, or converts it step by step through earlier forms. Scope rule D1 of the last-message fix (remote and unpaired sessions kept master's behaviour beside the new owner path) is the pattern to avoid; not retroactive; finishing it is w-5dae8178b905.
- Not to be read in: nothing about which peers or protocol versions are supported. No permission to discard persisted data or authority: carrying existing data forward under the one new mechanism is not keeping two (Architect2's qualifier). No authority to delete code without the usual gate, review and evaluation; it does not decide the size of any removal.

PRIORITIES [P19-P22]
- Finish evaluation work first [P19]: a relayed word; it sets priority and carries no commit authority. Finish line: the acceptance-evaluation loop working on real work under TermAl without workarounds. 2026-10-01 order: the conversation P0 (w-1b692f268123), then the evaluation cluster ahead of other work, including the first extraction (w-8597a0e17af3). Check the tracker for current state.
- Portable handoff and distributed work stay fully stopped [P20]: no TermAl work on them starts or continues until Greg is told, only through Engram::Advisor, that the council is ready, and takes it up. "Ready" means a considered, concrete design direction with its open questions clarified; exploratory activity is not ready.
- The session-blocking defect stays top priority until reproduced, fixed and independently verified [P21-P22]; see live-workarounds.

WHAT THESE WORDS DO NOT CHANGE
- They grant no other authority. Commit, push, install, restart and deploy rules stand as CLAUDE.md states them, including the reservation of restart, deploy and global configuration to Greg's explicit word.
- Authority text keeps (a), (b) and (c); (b) means sending him the exact wording and its consequence before the landing, not waiting for an answer. A widening of agent authority needs his recorded word.
- The "Work only in the repository folder" rule stands.
- Agents never end processes by hand, never restart the host, and never approve his approval cards. Greg still performs TermAl restarts himself. Do not generalize [P12] into unrelated process-control permissions (Advisor, with P12).
- An act that needs his explicit word waits until a sourced word exists; ask Engram::Advisor whether one does.
